title: Building a Spore-inspired evolution and tribe game in Godot 4
author: Ouvolk
selftext:
Hey everyone! I’ve been working on Primordium, a Spore-inspired evolution and tribe game built in Godot 4.

One of the biggest hurdles with AI gamedev in 3D is that rigging and skinning arbitrary creatures in external 3D tools doesn't fit an agent workflow. Instead, we built the entire creature pipeline procedurally in GDScript and shaders:

Procedural rig and skin: the skeleton and a single skin mesh are built from the creature’s spine and limb design, with foot planting via IK and the body leaning into turns.

Procedural parts: curved Bézier horns, tapered ears, bi-lobed tail clubs, wings you can glide with, and shader eyes with blinking eyelids.

Living ecosystem and tribe stage: herds follow a daily schedule (sleeping in nests at night, stretching at dawn, resting at midday), and later you found a tribe whose members gather, hunt, defend and play instruments.

For the AI workflow, the two things that helped the most were:

\- A headless capture script that renders the creature editor, world, and tribe stage to PNGs so the model can visually inspect its own 3D geometry changes.

\- A headless test suite and 5 AI bot players that simulate full runs of the creature and tribe stages to verify nothing broke after each change.

You can try the free demo on [itch.io](http://itch.io), and follow the Kickstarter pre-launch page for more GIFs and screenshots and to get notified when it goes live:

Demo: [https://akinjigames.itch.io/primordium](https://akinjigames.itch.io/primordium)

Kickstarter: [https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/primordium/primordium-evolve-your-own-creature-from-a-single-cell](https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/primordium/primordium-evolve-your-own-creature-from-a-single-cell)

Happy to answer questions and honest feedback!
